pr_title: Parse `-r` and `-c` entries as relative to containing file
pr_body:
## Summary

In a `requirements.txt` file, it turns out that the `-c` and `-r` entries should be interpreted as relative to the file in which they're declared, while the `-e` entries should be interpreted as relative to the current working directory, no matter where they're defined.

Previously, we always used the current working directory; now, we use the declaring file's directory for `-c` and `-r`.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/1367.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/1416.

issue_context.title: Included requirements files should be relative to parent, not cwd
issue_context.body:
```
. λ rm -rf tmp
. λ mkdir tmp
. λ cd tmp
./tmp λ printf 'mypy' > a.in                     
./tmp λ printf '-r a.in\nruff' > b.in
./tmp λ cd ..
. λ pip-compile --no-header --no-annotate tmp/b.in
WARNING: --strip-extras is becoming the default in version 8.0.0. To silence this warning, either use --strip-extras to opt into the new default or use --no-strip-extras to retain the existing behavior.
mypy==1.8.0
mypy-extensions==1.0.0
ruff==0.2.1
typing-extensions==4.9.0
. λ uv pip compile --no-header --no-annotate tmp/b.in
error: Error parsing included file in `tmp/b.in` at position 0
  Caused by: failed to open file `./a.in`
  Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

Ahh, I see, it's just files (not directories): https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8765

Looks like pip is inconsistent, in that in the following case it is relative to cwd:
